statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 10% with the overnight Nasdaq-100 futures band unchanged for a second consecutive hour and no new extreme set.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays EA_ON. The 13:00-15:00 UTC window spanning the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech is the session's main checkpoint, and the published forecast reaches WATCH there. The Bank of Japan governor's remarks at 06:35 UTC are a nearer checkpoint whose transmission runs through the yen and yields. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ edges back toward the top of an unchanged 102-point overnight band without setting a new high, leaving mean reversion intact into the Ueda remarks
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 31,384.50, up 66.75 points (+0.21%) from the 31,317.75 previous close. Price sits 75.25 points above the 31,309.25 overnight low and 26.75 below the 31,411.25 Globex high, inside a 102.00-point band worth about 0.33% of index value. The decisive observation for the Tail score is that the band is now unchanged across two consecutive hourly assessments: price drifted roughly 22 points higher from the midpoint over the past hour and stopped short of the high rather than breaking it. An approach to a boundary that is refused, following an earlier push to the same high that was given back, is working mean reversion rather than the persistent no-retracement path this score exists to detect. Tail therefore stays in the low band at 10%, a point above the prior hour only because price is now pressing the upper edge and E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,838.25 sit at the top of a narrow 9.50-point range, and because the Bank of Japan governor's remarks at 06:35 UTC are an unresolved checkpoint inside the current clock hour. VIX at 15.52 against a 15.31 prior close shows no bid for protection. The Asian handover offers no aligned directional lead, with the Nikkei up 0.3% and the Hang Seng up 0.8% against a 0.8% fall in Korea. Governor Ueda speaks at the National Securities Convention for the first time since the policy rate was lifted to 1.25% last month, with an October follow-up hike priced at roughly one chance in four and about 60% by year-end; the transmission to NQ runs through the yen and JGB yields rather than directly, and the content is unknown at assessment time. The equity backdrop is genuinely strong: the cash Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 31,076.44, up 268.51 points (+0.87%), in a 30,798.42-31,117.36 range, led by semiconductors as Nvidia set a record near a 6 trillion dollar valuation while Intel fell on Terafab discussions with TSMC. That record close is context for what an opening auction may test later today, not evidence of present structure, and the published forecast treats it as a conditional checkpoint at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC. The live concern remains in fixed income. The 10-year yield stands at 5.31%, up from a 5.28% prior close and near its highest since 2007, against H.15 readings of 4.83% at two years and 5.63% at thirty years, and Deutsche Bank has explicitly flagged that bonds and equities are pricing different worlds while indexes sit near records. Brent near 100 dollars with WTI at 88.90, down 0.59% in an 88.90-90.05 range, keeps energy an inflation input, though Aramco's warning that rebuilding thin inventories could take two years with Hormuz flows at 76% of prewar levels describes a slow supply recovery rather than a new discontinuity, and gold at 4,153.50 is marginally lower. None of that has transmitted into a one-way index path, so it is carried in Stress at 46% rather than in Tail. Confidence is 86%: current futures levels and ranges, the cash close, VIX, the 10-year yield, the H.15 curve, oil, gold, the Asian session, the Ueda speech schedule and a verified seven-day U.S. calendar were gathered directly from primary sources this run, with the shared Finviz context file the one input unavailable because its latest collection is roughly seven days stale and its collection status is partial, so it was excluded as supporting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the low Tail band apart from the 19:00 UTC hour on 5 October, which reached WATCH at 20% during the U.S. afternoon advance to a record close. Tail ran from 6% at 08:00 UTC through the European and U.S. sessions to that 20% peak, then decayed to 9% by 00:00 UTC, printed 12% at 01:00 UTC on a new Globex high and settled between 8% and 10% through 05:00 UTC. Stress fell steadily from 51% to 45% as realised volatility compressed even while long-end yields stayed near multi-decade highs, and Confidence held between 86% and 89% throughout. The 06:00 UTC hour on 5 October has no published assessment and is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 forecast hours and reaches WATCH only at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, which span the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech. Tail holds at 10-13% through the European session, steps to 14% as the weekly ADP release and the trade balance land at 12:15 and 12:30 UTC, peaks at 20% across the first two U.S. cash hours, then decays through the afternoon with a secondary 17% reading in the power hour before easing to 10-11% across the Asian session on 7 October. Stress tracks the same shape between 45% and 54%, and Confidence declines from 86% to 77% as distance from the verified overnight price evidence grows. Every hour beyond the current clock hour is conditional: no European or U.S. price path has been observed at assessment time, and the scheduled items in the event calendar are checkpoints rather than assertions about outcomes. The 10-year auction and the FOMC minutes fall on 7 October, after this window closes.
